props.title: Never Enough
lines: The hardest financial skill is stopping when you already have enough.
Do not risk what you have and need for what you do not have and do not need.

props.title: Gupta and Madoff

left.name: Rajat Gupta
lines: Reported net worth about $100 million. The book: that throws off roughly $600 an hour, 24 hours a day.
Still passed insider tips. Rajaratnam made a quick $1 million.
Prosecutors: Gupta's tips linked to about $17 million in profits. Gupta went to prison.

right.name: Bernie Madoff
lines: Legal market-making: about $25 to $50 million a year before the fraud.
Book: Madoff's electronic volume equaled about 9% of the New York exchange.
That legal business was not enough. The Ponzi is what people remember. Others were ruined.

props.note: Do not risk what you have and need for what you do not have and do not need.

rows.v: A rookie baseball player on $500,000 a year is rich in any normal life.
Mike Trout: 12-year, $430 million contract — about $36 million a year. The rookie can feel broke.
To feel like a top earner, the book says you might need $340 million in one year.
Some managers earned at least $770 million in 2018.
Jeff Bezos's net worth increased by about $24 billion in 2018 — the ladder has no last rung.

props.title: The antidote
items: Decide what enough is before results inflate your expectations.
Enough is people you will not disappoint, plus risk that lets you stay in the game.
Rockefeller, asked how much is enough: 'Just a little bit more' — a warning, not a plan.
If expectations rise with every win, compounding cannot catch a moving finish line.

rows.v: The book: a fortune that size generates almost $600 an hour, 24 hours a day.
Gupta still wanted the next rung. Comparison, not poverty, drove the extra risk.
Twenty-five to fifty million a year, legally, was already 'enough' by any household standard. It was not enough for his identity.
There is no reason to risk what you have and need for what you do not have and do not need.

props.title: Write enough before the ladder moves
items: A rookie on five hundred thousand can feel poor next to a three hundred forty million year.
Gupta already had a one hundred million fortune. The extra risk was comparison, not rent.
Madoff already had a legal fortune. The fraud was identity, not necessity.
Name the people you will not disappoint. That list is a better finish line than a neighbor's net worth.
